newsitem.title: SPAIN: BoS stresses relevance of peseta stability.
newsitem.headline: BoS stresses relevance of peseta stability.

text.p: Exchange rate stability is of great relevance for price convergence, according to the Bank of Spain's 1997 report, presented by Governor Luis Angel Rojo to a parliamentary committee on Tuesday.
The central bank set a 1997 inflation target of around 2.5 percent and a 1998 target of around two percent.

"Exchange rate stability (..) will be considered as a factor of great relevance for the convergence of Spanish inflation towards (inflation) in the more stable European Union countries," the report said.
The Bank of Spain added it is also important to keep inflation under control to "maintain the stability of the peseta".
The central bank added that M4 growth of below seven percent during 1997 will be consistent with the inflation target and economic growth for the coming year.
"From 1997, M4 growth below seven percent, with a medium term horizon, will be considered coherent with the expected downtrend in inflation and with stable economic growth," the report explained.
From next year the Bank of Spain is also planning to use private debt as collateral in the central bank's money market operations.
"During 1997 the Bank of Spain plans to start accepting private notes of high quality and liquidity, in these operations.
Even though these will be of a limited amount initially, this aims to adapt current tactics to the future European central banking system," the report said.
